title: On the Epistemic Uncertainty of Overparametrized Neural Networks
anchored_claims: Overparametrized one-hidden-layer ReLU networks (M>M* neurons) exhibit continuous non-identifiability through weight-splitting, where redundant neurons split a true neuron's contribution via coefficients constrained to a simplex, in addition to the discrete permutation symmetries present in exactly-specified models (Section 3.1, Section 3.2, Corollary 2).

Because standard information-theoretic uncertainty measures fail on these non-identifiable parameters, epistemic uncertainty is instead defined via the trace of the posterior weight covariance, EU(y|x) := tr(Cov_P(w|·)), enabling a variance-based decomposition into discrete (permutation) and continuous (splitting) sources of residual uncertainty (Section 2.1, Section 2.2, Example 1).

For one-hidden-layer ReLU networks, Theorem 1 characterizes the induced posterior over splitting coefficients as following symmetric Dirichlet distributions with concentration parameter alpha=(p+1)/2 (Lemma 4), with posterior means of individual redundant neurons scaling as O(M^-1/2) and within-neuron covariance remaining constant while cross-neuron covariance decays as O(M^-1) (Theorem 1, Corollary 1, Section 3.2).

The posterior over splitting coordinates remains non-degenerate even as the number of training samples n approaches infinity, showing that substantial parameter-space uncertainty persists despite the underlying function being fully identified (Section 3.2, Figure 2).
